selection_rationale: 34 candidates generated (IP-Adapter conditioned on the single fixed ref_002 anchor + style LoRA, varied prompt/seed per candidate, no ControlNet). All 34 held costume consistency (same green coat, white gloves, dark boots) -- the hypothesis this card tests. 5 were dropped: 3 near-duplicate front-view-idle repeats with no new view/pose information, and 2 for head-region rendering defects (a block-shaped head artifact, and a rigid visor/helmet that broke from the soft-hood silhouette established everywhere else). The kept 29 are not uniform camera angles -- IP-Adapter mostly kept generations front-facing regardless of the prompted angle -- but they are genuinely varied in pose, framing, and incidental detail (walking stride, arm gestures, hood up/down, close medium shots), which is real information the 12-image v1 set (2 camera angles x mirrors) did not have.
